content:
- Model consistently underestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially when history shows recent upward momentum.
- Forecasts tend to overshoot after sharp price spikes in the history, then correct downward — model should cap upward momentum corrections.
- Model exhibits persistent lag in capturing recent price reversals; true outcomes often turn up or down faster than forecasted.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized — model overweights recent highs/lows, fails to smoothly regress toward historical mean.
- Forecast horizon-specific bias: 30-day forecasts are too conservative early in the cycle, overcorrecting downward when prices are trending up.
- Model fails to adjust for seasonal or calendar-driven price patterns (e.g., post-holiday or pre-announcements) — should incorporate event-based heuristics.
- When history shows volatility clustering, model smooths too much — should allow for sharper, more volatile transitions in forecast.
- Forecast errors are more pronounced when history includes a recent sharp drop — model tends to underestimate the depth of the drop.
